problem:
Given that for $s>\omega ,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}},\,L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

find the Laplace transform of $f(t)=6\operatorname{cosh}⁡(10t)+\operatorname{sinh}⁡(10t)$ for $s>10.$

feedback.problem:
Given that for $s>\omega ,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}},\,L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\omega t)}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}},\end{aligned}
$$

find the Laplace transform of $f(t)=4\operatorname{cosh}⁡(8t)+3\operatorname{sinh}⁡(8t)$ for $s>8.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The linearity property of the Laplace transform states that for functions $f(t)$ and $g(t),$ we have

$$
L{\alpha f(t)+\beta g(t)}=\alpha \cdot L{f(t)}+\beta \cdot L{g(t)},
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants.

Taking the Laplace transform and applying the linearity property, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}L{4\operatorname{cosh}⁡(8t)+3\operatorname{sinh}⁡(8t)} & =L{4\operatorname{cosh}⁡(8t)}+L{3\operatorname{sinh}⁡(8t)} \\  & =4L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(8t)}+3L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(8t)}.\end{aligned}
$$

We are given that

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(\omega t)} & =\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>\omega , \\ L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(\omega t)} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-{\omega }^{2}}, &  & s>\omega .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(8t)} & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}-64},\,s>8 \\ L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(8t)} & =\frac{8}{{s}^{2}-64},\,s>8\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Laplace transform of $f(t)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L{f(t)} & =4L{\operatorname{cosh}⁡(8t)}+3L{\operatorname{sinh}⁡(8t)} \\  & =4\cdot \frac{s}{{s}^{2}-64}+3\cdot \frac{8}{{s}^{2}-64} \\  & =\frac{4s}{{s}^{2}-64}+\frac{24}{{s}^{2}-64} \\  & =\frac{4s+24}{{s}^{2}-64}.\end{aligned}
$$
